housing: Sutton is a mainly suburban borough of interwar semis and terraces, with older Victorian cottages in Carshalton and the large St Helier cottage estate on the Merton border. Home ownership is high (64.4% in 2021) and private renting is below the London average, at 20.3% of households. Sutton town centre has the most flats, including office-to-flat conversions and new blocks, and the borough’s grammar schools draw families who rent whole houses.
checkinTips: Interwar semis: photograph garages, side passages, gates and fences, and the condition of the front and back gardens.
Bay windows and older double glazing: photograph seals, handles and locks, and any mist between the panes.
Extensions and loft conversions are common: photograph ceilings and corners for cracks or damp staining, and note rooflights.
Town-centre flats, including converted offices: photograph the communal entrance, lift, post boxes and bin store, and record fob and key counts.
Older cottages in Carshalton: photograph solid walls and floors for damp, and any open fireplaces or wood burners.
Photograph the boiler, stopcock and meters, and test and photograph each smoke and carbon monoxide alarm.
tenantHelp: Sutton Council’s private sector housing service can inspect privately rented homes for disrepair and hazards; tenants can contact it through the council’s housing pages.
